text:
Alex Ovechkin keeps adding to the record book while the goals stay away. His assist on Boone Jenner's goal against Buffalo on Nov. 19 was the 763rd of his career, passing Nicklas Backstrom for the most in Capitals history, as NHL.com's Tom Gulitti noted. The same week, CBS Sports wrote that he is "Struggling to contribute in 2026-27," and Defector ran "Alex Ovechkin Is A Tough Watch These Days."

Both are fair. At 41 he has 1 goal and 7 points in 21 games on 13:37 a night, and no goals in his last 16. But those 16 games carried 4.5 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and for the season he has 5.6 expected against that single goal, a 2.7% shooting rate. We flag him as due, and his shot is still in the 97th percentile for speed in NHL Edge tracking.

The skating is the harder truth: his top speed sits at the bottom of the league, and he hasn't logged a single 20 mph burst. Washington has lost its last five. Whether the chances keep finding him is the thing to watch.
